name: Reprocess surgical instruments and scopes
function: surgical and perioperative services (medical device reprocessing)
summary: Used surgical instruments and flexible endoscopes come back from the operating rooms and endoscopy suites and the medical device reprocessing department cleans, inspects, assembles, packages, sterilizes or high-level disinfects and stores them for the next case. Technicians work around the clock to Canadian standards that require cleaning before sterilization, inspection of every instrument, recorded sterilizer loads, daily biological testing and quarantine of implant loads. Missing instruments, wet or torn packs, scarce sets needed twice in a day and surges at the end of the operating day are the main causes of delay and of incomplete trays reaching the OR.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with a medical device reprocessing department at each hospital, about 60 reprocessing technicians on rotating shifts, pass-through washer-disinfectors, steam and low-temperature sterilizers and paper count sheets or an instrument tracking system.
baseline.notes: Practice follows the PIDAC best practices (2013), which apply the CSA Z314 standards; Accreditation Canada surveys reprocessing against its standards.

unit_of_work: one instrument tray (or one flexible endoscope)
trigger: A surgical case or endoscopy ends and the used instruments or scope are contained for return to reprocessing.
end_state: The sterile tray is opened and accepted for the next case (or the scope is hung ready for use, or sent for repair).

volume.seasonality: Follows OR and endoscopy volumes: lower in summer and late December, very low in spring 2020; daily peaks in the afternoon and evening when lists finish.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate of about 2.5 trays per surgical or endoscopy case; kept unchanged. Dividing 9,500 trays by about 5,000 surgical and endoscopy cases gives about 1.9 per case, so the volume is plausible if some cases use several trays and some none.

Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35: about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead; physicians at estimated gross clinical earnings) from the organisation file. Most of the 60 reprocessing technicians on rotating shifts; the rest of their time is case cart assembly for other areas, sterile storage restocking and quality checks.

Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35: about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead; physicians at estimated gross clinical earnings) from the organisation file. Point-of-use containment and cart transport between the ORs and reprocessing; per-tray minutes are a share of handling a whole case cart.

Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35: about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead; physicians at estimated gross clinical earnings) from the organisation file. Checking and reporting trays at opening.

roles.title: Patient care manager, perioperative or surgical unit

evidence.note: Title, layer and loaded cost (wage x 1.35: about 25% benefits and HOOPP pension plus 10% overhead; physicians at estimated gross clinical earnings) from the organisation file. Reprocessing manager or supervisor oversight, audits and recall decisions, not modelled as steps; the organisation file has no separate reprocessing supervisor role.

systems.name: Instrument tracking system or paper count sheets and sterilizer load logs
Operating room scheduling and perioperative documentation module
Safety incident and complaints reporting system
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones

steps.name: Pre-clean and contain instruments at the point of use
steps.description: At the end of the case the OR attendant wipes gross soil off the instruments, opens hinged instruments, removes sharps, sprays the trays with enzymatic foam or covers them with a moist towel so soil does not dry, and closes them in the soiled case cart.

error.defect_description: Soil left to dry because the cart waits too long, making cleaning harder.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): keep soiled devices moist and contained

evidence.note: If cleaning cannot be done immediately, devices shall be kept moist; sterile and soiled items shall not be transported together (pidac2013, citing CSA Z314.8). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take the soiled cart to decontamination
steps.description: The attendant pushes the closed soiled case cart through the soiled corridor or dedicated elevator to the reprocessing department's decontamination area. Carts are often taken in batches at the end of a list.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): soiled devices transported in closed containers separate from sterile supplies

evidence.note: Soiled items travel in closed carts by a route separate from clean items (pidac2013); batching and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Receive, sort and disassemble
steps.description: In the decontamination room the reprocessing technician, in gown, gloves and face shield, checks the tray against its count sheet, separates delicate and powered instruments and scopes, and takes apart instruments that come apart.

error.defect_description: An instrument missing from the returned tray is not noticed.

evidence.note: Personal protective equipment and written procedures for reprocessing (pidac2013); the share of scopes is the author's estimate from the organisation file's endoscopy volume.

steps.name: Clean manually and in the ultrasonic washer
steps.description: The technician brushes lumens and box locks under water, flushes cannulated instruments and runs delicate instruments through the ultrasonic cleaner, following each manufacturer's instructions.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): cleaning before disinfection or sterilization according to the manufacturer's instructions

evidence.note: Cleaning steps and ultrasonic solution changes at least daily (pidac2013); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the washer-disinfector cycle
steps.description: The technician loads the instrument racks into a pass-through washer-disinfector, which washes, rinses, thermally disinfects and dries them and releases them on the clean side.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of cycle times for pass-through washer-disinfectors (about 45-75 minutes).

steps.name: Inspect and function-test on the clean side
steps.description: On the clean side the technician inspects every instrument under a lighted magnifier for residual soil, corrosion and damage, checks hinges, tips and insulation, and lubricates as required.

error.defect_description: A damaged or still-soiled instrument passes inspection.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): inspection of every device after cleaning

next.condition: residual soil or damage: reclean or replace

evidence.note: Inspection is a required step after cleaning and its results are recorded (pidac2013); the 5% reclean rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assemble the tray against the count sheet
steps.description: The technician lays out the tray following the count sheet or tracking screen, places each instrument in its place, adds an internal chemical indicator and notes any instrument that is missing or was swapped.

error.defect_description: Wrong or missing instrument placed and not noted on the count sheet.

next.condition: an instrument is missing or out of service

evidence.note: Packing time averaged 17.7 seconds per instrument in a London, Ontario hospital's central processing department (chin2014), so trays of 20 to 100 instruments take about 6 to 30 minutes; internal chemical indicators in each package (pidac2013). The missing-instrument share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Find or replace a missing instrument
steps.description: The technician searches the returned carts and other trays, asks the OR for the missing piece or takes a spare from stock; if no spare exists the tray is labelled incomplete and the OR is told, or a replacement is ordered.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wrap or container, label and record the tray
steps.description: The technician wraps the tray in sterilization wrap or places it in a rigid container, adds the external indicator and a label with tray name, sterilizer and load number, and records the tray in the load log or tracking system.

error.defect_description: Label or load record missing, breaking traceability.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): each package labelled and each load recorded for recall and patient tracing

evidence.note: All devices in each processed load must be recorded so they can be traced to patients in a recall (pidac2013); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the sterilization cycle
steps.description: When a load is full the technician loads the steam sterilizer (or a low-temperature sterilizer for heat-sensitive items) and starts the cycle; the first load of the day follows the air removal test and daily biological indicator test.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): daily air removal and biological indicator testing of sterilizers

evidence.note: A biological indicator tests each sterilizer each day it is used and each cycle type, and dynamic air removal sterilizers have a daily air removal (Bowie-Dick) test (pidac2013); cycle and load-filling times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Cool, unload and check the cycle record and indicators
steps.description: After the load cools the technician checks the printout for time, temperature and pressure, signs it, checks the external indicators and looks for wet packs before releasing the load.

error.defect_description: A wet or failed pack is released.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): signed review of each load's physical and chemical monitoring before release

next.condition: load contains implants: quarantine for the biological indicator
wet pack or failed parameter: repackage and resterilize

evidence.note: The load printout is signed to verify time, temperature and pressure, and loads with implants are quarantined until the biological indicator result (pidac2013); the shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold an implant load until the biological indicator reads
steps.description: The load stays in quarantine until the biological indicator from the load reads negative; the technician then records the result and releases it. A positive result triggers a recall of the load.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): implant loads released only after a negative biological indicator

evidence.note: Each load containing implantable devices is quarantined pending the biological indicator result (pidac2013); incubation times of 1 to 3 hours for rapid readers and up to 24 hours for older indicators are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Put the tray in sterile storage
steps.description: The technician places the tray on its labelled shelf in the sterile storage room, rotating stock so older trays are used first.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Pick the case cart for the next scheduled case
steps.description: The evening before, the technician picks each case's trays and supplies against the OR schedule's pick list and preference card and puts them on the case cart.
inputs: pick list from the OR schedule

error.defect_description: Wrong tray picked for the case.

next.condition: tray still in process or needed again the same day

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the wait is the time a tray spends on the shelf before its next scheduled use.

steps.name: Expedite a tray needed the same day
steps.description: The technician pulls the tray through washing, assembly and a priority sterilizer load ahead of the queue; for a single dropped instrument the OR may use immediate-use steam sterilization, which is logged to the patient.

control.basis: PIDAC best practice (2013): immediate-use steam sterilization only in emergencies, never for implants or complete sets, recorded to the patient

evidence.note: Immediate-use steam sterilization is for emergencies only, not for complete sets or implants, and is recorded with the patient's name, procedure and device; scheduling and lack of instruments do not justify it (pidac2013).

steps.name: Deliver the case cart to the operating room
steps.description: The OR attendant takes the case cart through the clean corridor or elevator to the operating room core before the case starts.

evidence.note: Sterile and soiled items are not transported together (pidac2013); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Open the tray and check sterility in the OR
steps.description: The OR nurse checks the external indicator, wrapper or container seal and dryness, opens the tray, checks the internal indicator and counts the instruments; a defective tray is set aside.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): check package integrity and indicators before use

next.condition: wet, torn, wrong, incomplete or indicator failed

evidence.note: Indicators show process failures such as incorrect packaging or loading (pidac2013); the 4% defect share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Leak test and manually clean the endoscope
steps.description: For a flexible endoscope the technician performs the leak test before cleaning, then brushes and flushes every channel with detergent following the manufacturer's instructions.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013) (Z314.8 and endoscope provisions): leak test and manual cleaning before high-level disinfection

evidence.note: Leak testing after each use and before cleaning; a scope that fails the dry leak test should not be immersed (pidac2013); minutes and failure share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the automated endoscope reprocessor
steps.description: The technician connects the cleaned scope to an automated endoscope reprocessor, which runs a high-level disinfection cycle with a monitored disinfectant concentration, then rinses and air-purges every channel.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a 25-45 minute reprocessor cycle; the wait is for a free reprocessor.

steps.name: Dry, record and hang the endoscope
steps.description: The technician dries the channels, records the scope's serial number, the reprocessor cycle and the patient it was used on, and hangs it vertically in the ventilated storage cabinet.

control.basis: CSA Z314 series (Canadian medical device reprocessing standards) as applied in PIDAC Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization (2013): endoscope storage and reprocessing record linked to the patient

evidence.note: Endoscopes are stored hanging vertically in a dedicated, closed, ventilated cabinet, with a permanent record tracking endoscopes and patients (pidac2013).

steps.name: Send a failed endoscope for repair
steps.description: The technician tags the scope out of service, records the failure and arranges repair with the manufacturer or biomedical engineering; the endoscopy unit is told it is down a scope.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Report the defective tray and send it back
steps.description: The OR nurse files a report in the incident system or on the defect slip, and the tray goes back to decontamination to be fully reprocessed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; incomplete trays are named as a frequent incident in the organisation file.

exceptions.name: Missing or out-of-service instrument at assembly
exceptions.description: An instrument is missing from the returned tray or fails inspection; the technician searches, substitutes or flags the tray incomplete.

exceptions.name: Implant load quarantine
exceptions.description: Loads with implants are held until the biological indicator reads negative.

exceptions.name: Tray needed again the same day
exceptions.description: A scarce set is booked twice in a day or not yet processed, so it is expedited through a priority load.

exceptions.name: Defective tray found in the OR
exceptions.description: The tray is wet, torn, incomplete or has a failed indicator and returns for full reprocessing.

exceptions.name: Endoscope fails leak test
exceptions.description: About 3% of scopes (12% of items) fail the leak test and go out for repair.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from end of case to the tray being opened for its next case
benchmarks.population: Community hospital reprocessing, mixed instrument trays

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 4-6 hours of processing from decontamination to sterile storage, then typically one day on the shelf before the next scheduled use; little-used sets wait several days.

benchmarks.population: Central processing department, St Joseph's Hospital, London, Ontario, 2013

evidence.note: Instrument utilization averaged 27.8% of instruments on the tray.

pain_points.description: Trays carry many instruments that are rarely used, so assembly and inspection time is spent on instruments that are opened and returned unused.

evidence.note: Average instrument utilization of 27.8% and a 57% possible tray reduction in otolaryngology (chin2014).

pain_points.description: Missing or swapped instruments make trays incomplete; the OR finds them only when the tray is opened.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; incomplete trays are named as a frequent incident in the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Soiled carts arrive in a rush when lists finish in the afternoon, while morning trays must be ready by 07:30, so evening shifts carry the peak and scarce sets get expedited.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Implant loads wait for biological indicator results before release, and loaner sets that arrive late from vendors cannot be released in time.

evidence.note: Implant load quarantine rule (pidac2013).

sources.title: Best Practices for Cleaning, Disinfection and Sterilization of Medical Equipment/Devices in All Health Care Settings, 3rd edition (May 2013)
sources.publisher: Provincial Infectious Diseases Advisory Committee (PIDAC), Public Health Ontario
sources.supports: Reprocessing steps and requirements: keep soiled devices moist, separate transport, cleaning before sterilization, inspection, internal and external indicators, load records and traceability, daily biological indicator and air removal tests, implant load quarantine, restrictions on immediate-use steam sterilization, endoscope leak testing and storage; references to CSA Z314.

sources.title: Reducing otolaryngology surgical inefficiency via assessment of tray redundancy (Chin et al.), Journal of Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery (full text via Europe PMC, PMC4263198)
sources.publisher: Journal of Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery (BioMed Central)
sources.supports: Tray packing time of 17.7 seconds per instrument and 27.8% instrument utilization in an Ontario hospital.

assumptions: One unit of work is one tray or scope; a case usually returns several trays, and the organisation file's 9,500 trays a month is kept.

Point-of-use pre-cleaning for endoscopes is done by the endoscopy nurse and for loaner sets is not needed; the labour of step s01 is attributed to the OR attendant for all items, which slightly overstates attendant time.
Washer-disinfectors and automated endoscope reprocessors are not in the organisation file's resources; six of each across three sites is the author's estimate.
The organisation file has no instrument tracking system; it is added here as a workflow system covering either a tracking product or paper count sheets and load logs, both common in 2019-2022.

The simulated median is compared with an estimated benchmark only; the shelf wait (s15) is a triangular estimate of 4 hours to 3 days, mode 16 hours. The cycle time includes the time a tray waits on the sterile shelf for its next scheduled case (s15), which dominates the elapsed time; processing alone is about 4 to 6 hours.
Steam sterilizer cycle times of 45-90 minutes include drying; low-temperature cycles for heat-sensitive devices are folded into the same step.

Hands-on time x volume implies about 68 FTE against 60.5 stated; reprocessing technicians alone come to about 57 FTE at 130 productive hours, close to the organisation file's headcount of 60 people on rotating 24/7 shifts, which leaves little slack for case carts for other departments, restocking and audits. The simulated median (about 1.5 days) is about 1.4 times the estimated 1.1-day benchmark because of the shelf wait.
Vendor loaner sets that arrive from suppliers enter at decontamination like used trays; the organisation file's process map does not list suppliers as a trigger for this process.
